rejected_findings.reason: False premise: dispatch_signup_meta's 3rd parameter IS landlord_uuid by signature (auth_handler.gleam:1513-1518); the event_id is generated inside the function as uuid.v4_string(). The test comment is accurate about the recorded event_id value. No contract violation.

findings.title: Organic re-initiate does not clear a stale rt_first_touch cookie left by an abandoned attempt, so the callback attributes the new signup to the old attempt's params
findings.detail: Attempt 1 (paid landing) sets the cookie; user abandons at Google (no callback, no terminal clear); a second organic initiate within 300s hits the `[] -> response` branch which neither overwrites nor clears; the callback then locks the stale params via $set_once, contradicting the module's documented 'no cookie -> provider=google' guarantee.
findings.recommended_fix: In the `[] -> response` branch, also apply `first_touch_cookie.clear_cookie(response, req)` so every initiate is set-or-clear.

findings.title: '~4KB header budget' protection claim is false for non-ASCII values — clamp is grapheme-based, not byte-based
findings.evidence:
pub fn clamp_value(raw: String) -> String {
  raw
  |> string.trim
  |> string.slice(0, max_value_len)
findings.detail: Verified: stdlib string.slice is grapheme_slice (grapheme clusters, not bytes); uri.query_to_string percent-encodes each UTF-8 byte to %XX (3x). 8 keys x 200 four-byte graphemes => ~19KB percent-encoded, past the ~4KB cookie cap; browsers silently drop the Set-Cookie and attribution is lost (graceful provider=google fallback). The doc's budget claim only holds for ASCII.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp by encoded byte length before cookie_value(), or scope the doc comment to ASCII.

findings.title: Client-side OAuth initiate wiring (UserClickedGoogleSignIn -> query string) has no test
findings.detail: Verified: no client test references UserClickedGoogleSignIn (grep of client/test/). The #617 mechanism's only untested link; a wiring regression silently ships every OAuth signup unattributed — the exact bug this PR fixes. The client.update harness exists (client_test.gleam:164).
findings.recommended_fix: Add client.update tests for UserClickedGoogleSignIn: params present -> query on the initiate URI; empty params -> query None.

findings.title: find_set_cookie helper duplicated across six test files (three pre-existing — matches established convention)
findings.evidence: fn find_set_cookie(resp: wisp.Response, name: String) -> Result(String, Nil) {

findings.title: Initiate test claims the cookie payload is signed base64url but never asserts it — a wisp.Plain regression would pass
findings.detail: Verified: assertions check only name prefix and Max-Age; a Plain cookie containing the raw query string passes identically, while read_cookie(Signed) would silently return empty in production. The round-trip tests sign via simulate.cookie regardless of how the handler sets it, so nothing else guards the write being signed.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the cookie value contains no 'utm_' substring (or round-trip decode it) so a Plain regression fails the test.

findings.title: set_once_with_fallback doc claims 'no-op for returning sign-ins' but provider=google is new for every pre-deploy account
findings.evidence: /// for returning sign-ins (their original values are already locked).
findings.detail: Verified: pre-deploy OAuth signups locked an EMPTY $set_once set, so provider is not already locked for them; their next sign-in writes provider=google. The behavior is deliberate (PR body documents it as a backfill bonus) — only the doc comment misstates it.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the doc to state provider is written once to any account lacking it.

findings.title: First-touch attribution poisoning: unauthenticated /auth/oauth/google persists attacker-chosen UTM params into a signed cookie, locked into the victim's $set_once on their first Google signup
findings.detail: Verified: the public GET initiate route persists attacker-chosen query values on any top-level navigation (first-party Set-Cookie context; SameSite does not block it). Impact is attribution corruption only: values allow-listed, clamped, percent-encoded, signature-verified — no injection or forgery. The same poisoning class pre-exists via crafted landing URLs on the password path (#466); the endpoint is a slightly shorter path to the same surface.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept and document as inherent to URL-param attribution, or require a first-party signal (Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin) on initiate before persisting params.

findings.title: set_once_with_fallback hardcodes provider=google inside a provider-agnostic flow
findings.detail: Verified: complete_oauth_flow never learns the provider (token_resp has no provider field); the google literal is held correct only by allowed_oauth_providers = ["google"] (auth_handler.gleam:972). A second provider would silently misattribute.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass the provider into set_once_with_fallback (or thread it from the callback route) rather than hardcoding.

findings.title: first-touch cookie max-age is a second literal mirroring pkce_max_age, coupled by comment only
findings.detail: Verified: two 300 literals in separate modules, coupled only by the docstring 'same max-age as the PKCE verifier'. A future shortening of the PKCE window would silently leave the attribution cookie outliving the flow it tags.
findings.recommended_fix: Reference one shared constant (export pkce_max_age or move both windows into a shared auth module).

findings.title: Attribution key list triplicated (client extractor, signup_decoder, first_touch_cookie.keys) with no enforced sync
findings.detail: Verified: the same 8 keys live in client/src/helpers/first_touch.gleam, auth_handler.gleam:147-154 (signup_decoder), and first_touch_cookie.keys, joined only by comments. Adding a key to the decoder but not the cookie module silently drops OAuth attribution for it.
findings.recommended_fix: Define the server key list once (attribution.gleam, imported by first_touch_cookie) and add a unit test asserting cookie keys == signup body keys.

findings.title: OAuth callback error branches never exercised; the added clear_cookie calls are untested in situ
findings.detail: Verified: 8 clear_cookie call sites; only the success path (integration) and the function itself (unit) are pinned. Branches are pre-existing and untested; additions are one-liners of a unit-tested function — P3.
findings.recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is. If hardening: one test driving handle_oauth_callback with an error query param, asserting both first-touch and PKCE cookies expire.
